A typical rent of $1,325 is close to what Dearborn renters pay, even though owned homes here are worth far less. Rents that high against modest home values make rented houses common, so the city's rental registration rules come up in many sales.

Do Eastpointe rental and vacant property rules affect a sale?

They can. The Building Department manages registration and inspection of every non-owner-occupied residential property, and tenants cannot occupy a rental until the city certifies it. If your house is rented, the buyer inherits that regime.

  • Rentals must be registered and inspected every two years from the application date.
  • If a property is certified at the time of sale, the certificate may transfer to the new owner when that owner registers within 14 days of purchase.
  • Owners and property managers complete a one-time registration separate from the property registration.
  • An owner who lives 50 miles or more from city hall must name a local agent.
  • A furnace or boiler must pass an inspection by a qualified contractor.

Vacant buildings have their own rule: register inside 45 days of the vacancy, renew each year until the property is occupied again, and obtain a certificate of compliance for re-occupancy. Call the Building Department at 586-445-3661 for rentals (extension 2269) or vacant properties (extension 2214).

Which schools, roads and nearby colleges matter to Eastpointe buyers?

Eastpointe Community Schools reaches most parcels. It was called East Detroit Public Schools until 2017 and runs one high school, one middle school and four elementary schools. South Lake Schools claims the southeastern corner, and its Koepsell Elementary stands inside Eastpointe's borders. Confirm the district for your parcel before listing, since boundaries shape what a family will pay.

Gratiot Avenue (M-3) runs through the city, with I-94 and I-696 close by, and 8 Mile Road (M-102) and 9 Mile Road carry cross-town traffic. Macomb Community College's South Campus is two miles north in Warren, and the Wayne County Community College District's Mary Ellen Stempfle University Center is across 8 Mile Road in Harper Woods.

Local life centers on John F. Kennedy Memorial Park, the Cruisin' Gratiot car celebration in June and the late-July Erin-Halfway Days festival. The American Power Boat Association is headquartered in the city, and the first Art Van furniture showroom opened on Gratiot in 1959.

When are Eastpointe property taxes due?

The City Treasurer collects for the city, Macomb County, Macomb Community College, the intermediate school district, the state education tax and both school districts. About 30,000 bills go out each year, and both school districts ask that 100 percent of school tax appear on the summer bill.

  • Summer taxes are due July 1 with a September 1 deadline. Pay it all by September 1, or pay half by then and the other half by December 1.
  • Winter taxes are due December 1 with a February 15 deadline.
  • A summer balance left after September 1 grows by 1 percent a month, with 2 percent more from February 16.
  • A winter balance left after February 15 carries a 3 percent charge.
  • From March 1, unpaid taxes go to the Macomb County Treasurer at One South Main Street in Mount Clemens, with added penalties.

Eligible owners can defer summer taxes to February 15 if household income is $40,000 or less and they are 62 or older, disabled, a qualifying veteran, a surviving spouse or blind. The deferment application is due by September 15. For a payoff figure, call the taxes line at 586-445-3661, option 6.

What paperwork does the Eastpointe assessor handle after a sale?

Eastpointe's Assessing Department explains the sequence in plain terms. The buyer signs the principal residence exemption form at closing if the house will be owner-occupied. The seller signs a request to rescind the exemption and files it with the assessor, which clears the seller's name from the homestead and lets the seller claim it on the next home.

Buyers owe the assessor a Property Transfer Affidavit, due 45 days after the transfer. Each late day costs $5, capped at $200. The taxable value is uncapped the year after a transfer, so the new owner's bill rises to match the assessed value, which the city sets at half of market value.

An owner who thinks the value is too high must appear in March, since that is the only month the Board of Review hears opinions of value. The July and December sessions deal with clerical errors, mutual mistakes of fact and poverty requests. A homeowner who loses can take the case to the Michigan Tax Tribunal by June 30.

What state transfer taxes apply to an Eastpointe sale?

MCL 207.526 exempts, among others, a deed that does nothing but straighten a boundary line and a land contract that has not yet passed legal title. A land contract buyer can still claim the principal residence exemption if the contract is recorded or recordable.

Sign a request to rescind the exemption and file it with the Eastpointe Assessing Department. That clears your name from the homestead so you can claim the exemption on your next home.

A Property Transfer Affidavit, filed at the Assessor's Office. The closing agent usually supplies the form, but the buyer must file it, and a filing later than 45 days costs $5 per day up to $200.

What happens when you sell a Jackson house?

Jackson is the seat of Jackson County. A sale there involves city hall on West Michigan Avenue, which handles assessing, treasury and rental registration, and the county, which handles recording. The house can be listed, sold privately, or bought as-is by a cash buyer, and the legal steps at closing match in every case. What differs is the house's condition and whether an owner or tenants live in it.

Jackson grew around the junction of I-94 and US 127, roughly 35 miles west of Ann Arbor, 35 miles south of Lansing, 75 miles west of Detroit and 65 miles east of Kalamazoo. It covers about 10.96 square miles. Mid-2025 estimates count 31,022 people, a 0.9 percent slip from the 2020 base.

What shaped the Jackson market and its older neighborhoods?

Horace Blackman claimed land here in 1829, and Jackson became a village in 1843 and a city in 1857. A county convention held under the oaks on July 6, 1854 carries a state historical marker identifying it as the birth of the Republican Party. Before Detroit built cars on assembly lines in 1910, Jackson factories were already making parts and assembling them, and more than 20 car brands once came from the city.

Heavy industry restructured around mid-century, which cost jobs and population. Three major private employers stand out: CMS Energy, which keeps its headquarters downtown, Henry Ford Health and Eaton. Michigan's first prison opened here in 1838, and a state corrections complex still operates in the area. Railroads made Jackson the crossroads of Michigan, and the Michigan Central depot on East Michigan Avenue is reported as the nation's oldest train station in continuous active use. Amtrak's Wolverine stops three times daily in each direction.

How affordable are Jackson homes?

Jackson sits at the low end of all four cities for both prices and rents. Survey figures for 2020 through 2024:

  • Typical owner-occupied home value: $103,200.
  • Homeownership: 54.7 percent of 13,281 households.
  • Typical rent: $898 a month.
  • Household size averages 2.29, and 16.1 percent of adults have finished a bachelor's degree.
  • Average trip to work: 17.0 minutes.

With a typical value near $103,000 and almost half of households renting, many Jackson houses belong to investors or need repairs, so buyers will scrutinize roofs, furnaces and foundations. If repair costs exceed what they would add to the price, an as-is sale to a cash buyer may be the simpler path.

What happens to rental registration when a Jackson rental sells?

Jackson keeps a registry of rentals that are not owner-occupied, and a sale restarts it. A registration is good for 3 years, owners report changes within 10 days, and renewals are due no later than 60 days before expiry. Selling voids the registration, and the new owner applies at closing. Within 45 days after the sale, the seller of a rented dwelling tells the Community Development Department who bought it and where to reach them.

A buyer who claims a 100 percent principal residence exemption with the city assessor skips registration. Anyone else registers within 45 days of closing, with a $5 per unit daily penalty for lateness. Fees are not refunded or credited on a transfer, so a seller who just paid for a registration cannot recover it.

What is Jackson's payment calendar for property taxes?

City bills arrive July 1 (summer) and December 1 (winter). Pay the summer bill in a lump by July 31, or split it into five payments due on the 20th from July to November. The winter bill is open for payment December 1 to February 14. Dates from the assessor's calendar:

December 31Tax day: condition of the property on this date sets the next assessment

Source: City of Jackson Assessor important dates and Treasurer pages.

Why will a buyer's Jackson tax bill likely exceed mine?

Michigan limits yearly growth of taxable value to the lesser of 5 percent or inflation, until a sale lifts the limit. After a transfer of ownership, MCL 211.27a resets taxable value for the following calendar year to the state equalized value, roughly half of market value. A long-time owner's bill probably sits well below what the next owner pays, so mention this early to serious buyers.

Sellers should also file a rescission of their principal residence exemption within 90 days of moving out (MCL 211.7cc), sending the form to the Jackson assessor.

Which Jackson employers and landmarks help a listing?

  • Dawn Foods, family-owned, has been based in Jackson since 1920.
  • Michigan Automotive Compressor is described as the largest manufacturer in the county and its fourth-largest single employer.
  • Reynolds Field, a general aviation airport of about 700 acres south of I-94, hosts the Jackson College Flight School and the annual Jackson Blues Festival in June.
  • Cell Block 7 Prison Museum occupies a closed cell block that was reopened to visitors.

Buyers who commute to Lansing, Ann Arbor or Detroit weigh the drive on I-94 and US 127, so state the exit and the time to each in your listing.

Will the city income tax follow me after I sell in Jackson?

Jackson levies its own income tax. Residents with income over $600 file and pay 1 percent; people who commute in to work pay 0.5 percent; corporations and partnerships pay 1 percent. Returns are due April 30, or the next business day when that date lands on a weekend. If you sell and move out of town, ask the treasurer's office how a part-year return works.

What will transfer tax cost on a Jackson sale?

Two Michigan taxes fall on the seller at recording: the state's $3.75 per $500 of price and the county's 55 cents per $500 where the county has fewer than 2,000,000 people. At the $103,200 median value, the price rounds up to 207 units of $500, or $890.10. Jackson County's Register of Deeds allows transfer tax to be folded into the recording fee on a single check payable to that office.

MCL 207.526 also exempts gifts to a child or grandchild, title-correction deeds and security instruments, and the county register posts its own exemption guidance.

What can I expect from Jackson's weather and schools when showing a house?

Winters here run cold and summers warm. The average January low is 17.5 degrees, the lowest reading on record is minus 20, and snowfall averages 37.3 inches a year, so a furnace and roof in good shape are real selling points. Almost the whole city lies inside Jackson Public Schools, with Jackson College, Baker College and Spring Arbor University among the local colleges. The city's parks department runs 26 parks totaling 645 acres, and JATA buses run ten routes Monday through Saturday from a downtown station. Mention these in listings for buyers who ask about commutes and schools.

More questions about Jackson, MI

What must a Jackson landlord tell the city after a sale?

Notify Community Development within 45 days, with the buyer's name and address. The buyer registers within 45 days after closing, unless they file a 100 percent principal residence exemption.

When are Jackson summer property taxes due?

In full by July 31, or in five installments on the 20th of July through November. Winter taxes can be paid December 1 through February 14.

Does Jackson tax income?

Yes. Residents with more than $600 in income pay 1 percent and nonresident workers pay 0.5 percent, with returns due April 30.

What transfer tax applies to a $103,200 Jackson sale?

$890.10, since the price rounds up to 207 units of $500, each carrying $3.75 state and $0.55 county tax (county under 2,000,000 residents). The seller pays at recording.

What is the deadline for a new Jackson owner's principal residence exemption?

June 1 for the summer bill. The owner must own and occupy the home by then, and the July Board of Review can fix missed claims.

Much of Oak Park grew in the postwar boom described below, so a house often carries decades of updates, some permitted and some not. A buyer with a mortgage orders an inspection and an appraisal. Begin with what you control. Find your last deed, locate permit records for the roof, furnace and electrical work, and collect your utility account details.

How would you describe Oak Park to an out-of-town buyer?

Oak Park is a Detroit-bordering suburb about 14 miles northwest of downtown, and it covers 5.16 square miles, all of it land. Eight Mile Road (M-102) forms the south edge and doubles as the Oakland and Wayne county line. Eleven Mile Road bounds the north, Greenfield Road the west, and I-696 clips the northern edge, with the Lodge Freeway (M-10) nearby (Wikipedia, Oak Park).

The first major housing development went up in 1914. The village was incorporated in 1927 and the city on October 29, 1945. From 1950 to 1960 the population jumped from about 5,000 to above 36,000, and the city was called America's fastest growing. Parts of Royal Oak Township were annexed in 2002 and 2004. A FedEx distribution center on a 60-acre former armory site opened on March 31, 2017.

The Census Bureau estimates 29,072 residents for July 1, 2025, which is 1.7% below the 2020 base. At 5,743.2 people per square mile in 2020, Oak Park was more densely settled than Novi, Pontiac or Port Huron, so houses sit close together and street-level comparables carry weight.

  • Residents below the poverty line: 12.0%.

Each year the city assessor publishes a sales study. The 2026 assessment-year study draws on sales from April 1, 2023 through March 31, 2025, and an economic condition factor report can be looked up by parcel on BSAonline.com. Reading both shows how the assessor treats houses like yours, which helps when weighing an offer.

Which school district covers a given Oak Park address?

Oak Park Schools serves most of the city. Homes between 10 Mile and 11 Mile Roads belong to the Berkley School District, and about a square mile at the east end is in Ferndale Public Schools.

A boundary that follows a street means two neighbors can be in different districts. Check the exact address, especially in the strip near I-696 where Berkley applies.

The city lists separate building, electrical and demolition permits, and the Building Division at 14300 Oak Park Boulevard takes building applications. It also publishes Roofing Guidelines for Residential Properties describing the roofing permit and the inspections a roof job requires.

If a prior owner did the roof, wiring or an addition, ask Municipal Services what is on record for your address. A missing final sign-off is cheaper to resolve before listing than after a buyer's inspector spots it. City code also asks owners, occupants and tenants to maintain the ground around their buildings, so cut back overgrowth and haul out debris before showings. Oak Park also requires a building permit before any demolition of a residential or commercial structure, so a seller who wants to remove a damaged garage or shed should apply first.

Clearing out a home is part of many sales. A residential garage sale needs a $10 permit from the City Clerk's Office, which asks for a state ID or driver's license showing the sale address.

Which forms go to the Oak Park assessor after a sale?

The Assessor's Office is at 14000 Oak Park Boulevard. Two filings follow a sale.

  • Property Transfer Affidavit: needed whenever ownership changes, including title, beneficial use or ownership interest, with a 45-day deadline from the transfer.
  • Request to Rescind Principal Residence Exemption: filed by homeowners who sell or convert their principal residence so the exemption ends.

The buyer files a new exemption form after closing; the city lists it as Form 2368 and takes it at the same Assessor's Office counter. Ask your closing agent which of these it handles so none is filed twice or skipped.

How is an Oak Park deed recorded at the county level?

The deed goes to the Oakland County Register of Deeds. Its fee page lists the county transfer tax as 55 cents for each $500 of consideration and the state tax as $3.75 for each $500. Consideration under $100.00 is exempt, and the reason for any exemption has to be written on the face of the document.

The office's question list adds a few requirements you can check in advance: notarized signatures, a 2-1/2 inch blank top margin, and an embossed seal on any death certificate filed. Its index reaches back to January 1, 1964, so you can pull your own earlier deed and confirm the legal description before signing.

Is an inspection required before an Oak Park house is sold?

City pages list a certificate of occupancy for new or altered buildings and a rental inspection every two years or after a change in tenancy. Ask Municipal Services whether your house, particularly one that has been rented, needs either before a buyer moves in.

What does a certificate of occupancy cost in Oak Park?

The fee schedule prints $50 for occupancy only and $50 for reissuance. Commercial and renovation certificates carry different amounts on the same schedule.

Should an Oak Park seller do anything about the alarm permit?

The city's alarm page states a one-time $20 fee and says each change in ownership of an operable alarm system requires a new permit. Tell the buyer so they register the system in their own name.

What is the deadline for the Property Transfer Affidavit in Oak Park?

Forty-five days from the transfer, filed at the Assessor's Office, 14000 Oak Park Boulevard. It covers any change in title, beneficial use or ownership interest.

Where does the deed for an Oak Park house get filed?

At the Oakland County Register of Deeds. A warranty deed is first tax certified at the county treasurer's office for $5.00, and recording costs $30.00.

What are the realistic ways to sell in Port Huron?

Port Huron homeowners can put the house on the market with an agent, handle a private sale, or deal with a buyer who purchases houses outright. The city is the St. Clair County seat, so the county's land records office sits inside city limits.

How quickly a sale closes comes down to what is left unresolved. Clear title, permits on file and an empty house move fast on any route. An unpaid tax bill, a missing permit or a lease in place slows things, and the buyer either waits for a fix or discounts the price. The sections below cover what the city and county ask for, so you can clear those items early.

Where does Port Huron sit and what shapes its housing?

Port Huron stands where Lake Huron narrows into the St. Clair River, facing Sarnia, Ontario across the water. The Blue Water Bridge links the two cities at the eastern end of I-69 and I-94. The city's total area is 12.26 square miles, though only 8.08 of that is land, and the Black River splits the city in half before reaching the St. Clair near downtown (Wikipedia, Port Huron).

The U.S. built Fort Gratiot here in 1814, the city incorporated in 1857, and it became the county seat in 1871. A fire swept through on October 8, 1871, and an F4 tornado on May 21, 1953 damaged or destroyed over 400 structures. The village of Fort Gratiot was annexed in 1895. Shipbuilding and lumber work pulled in immigrants in the 1850s, and auto-parts makers followed later.

The 2020 census counted 28,983 residents. The Census Bureau's July 1, 2025 estimate is 28,273, a 2.4% decline. Over 8.10 square miles of land, density was 3,577.3 people per square mile.

NOAA's 1991 to 2020 normals give Port Huron 34.87 inches of precipitation and 35.5 inches of snow in a year, spread over 22 snowy days. January averages a low of 19.9 F, the record low is minus 19 F, and the July average high is 81.3 F.

With so much shoreline, flood mapping matters. The city's planning page links flood maps, and the building page says a property in a flood plain or zone may need EGLE Water Resources approval for exterior projects. Ask the Building Inspection Division whether your parcel is mapped before you list.

What draws buyers to Port Huron?

Water access is the main draw. The city owns 17 waterfront areas covering 102 acres with 3.5 miles of frontage, three public beaches and the largest municipal marina system in Michigan, with five mooring locations. It also has 14 public parks and a community center.

Work comes from auto-parts makers such as SMR Automotive and International Automotive Components, plus two acute care hospitals, McLaren Port Huron and Lake Huron Medical Center. St. Clair County Community College is in the city, and Port Huron High School and Port Huron Northern High School serve students.

It does. The planning department runs a Rental Certification Program, and its document center posts a Foreclosed, Vacant and Abandoned Property Registration Form. If your house has been rented or sits empty, ask the Building Inspection Division what registration or certification applies to the address and whether it passes to a buyer.

Houses inside the historic area fall under Chapter 52-576 through 52-591 of the city's Historic District ordinance, which requires a work permit for alterations, significant repairs, new construction, demolition and moving.

What happens at the St. Clair County land records office?

The register's office is at 200 Grand River Avenue, Suite 103, Port Huron, phone (810) 989-6930. Monday through Thursday it works from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Friday from 10:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., with a lunch closing from noon to 1:00 p.m. The recording counter shuts at 4:00 p.m., and anything received later is dated 8:00 a.m. on the next business day.

  • Recording charge: a flat $30.00 for each document whatever its page count, plus $3.00 after the first instrument reference.
  • Certified copy of a recorded document: $5.00.
  • Tax certificate: required before recording a warranty deed, a land contract, or any deed with a warranty covenant, under MCL 211.135. The treasurer certifies over the counter from 9:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m., closed noon to 1:00 p.m.
  • Transfer tax as the county's page prints it: $1.10 for each thousand dollars of sale amount for the county and $7.50 for each thousand for the state.

Land records can be viewed online from 1984 forward, and the office runs a Property Fraud Alert sign-up. Most sellers let the closing agent carry the deed in.

How soon can a Port Huron sale close?

It depends on title, taxes and any tenant. At the recording end, the St. Clair County counter closes at 4:00 p.m., and a document received after that is dated 8:00 a.m. the next business day.

Do I need a permit for work I did before selling in Port Huron?

Roofs, windows, doors, siding, decks, garages and basement finishes need a building permit, and furnaces, water heaters and sump pumps need trade permits. The city's page says skipping one can cause problems when you sell.

Where is a Port Huron deed recorded?

At the St. Clair County Register of Deeds, 200 Grand River Avenue, Suite 103. A warranty deed needs a county treasurer's tax certificate first.

What transfer tax does St. Clair County print?

The Register of Deeds fee page prints $1.10 per thousand dollars of sale amount for the county and $7.50 per thousand for the state. Your closing statement shows the exact dollar amounts for your sale.

Are there flood zones to check before listing in Port Huron?

Yes. The city links flood maps on its planning page, and a property in a flood plain may need state approval for exterior projects. Call the Building Inspection Division at (810) 984-9733 to learn whether your parcel is mapped.

What does a Hamtramck seller deal with first?

Hamtramck is a two-square-mile city in Wayne County that sits almost entirely inside Detroit's borders, so a sale here follows Hamtramck's own city code and Wayne County's tax process, which differ from Detroit's. Whether the house goes to market, to a neighbor, or to a cash buyer, it passes three local checkpoints: the city's pre-sale inspection rules, the treasurer's tax calendar, and the assessor's transfer paperwork.

The city covers 2.09 square miles, all of it land, and Interstate 75 runs roughly along its western edge with I-94 near the southern edge. Downtown Detroit is about 5 miles south. Census estimates for mid-2025 count 27,261 people, 4.1 percent fewer than the 2020 base. Expect sales to be decided block by block rather than by a citywide trend.

How did Hamtramck's housing stock come about?

Most of the older homes trace back to the factory boom. The Dodge Brothers plant opened in 1914, and Hamtramck's population jumped by more than 1,200 percent between 1910 and 1920 as workers moved close to the line. The village became a city in 1922, partly to resist annexation by Detroit. Around 1925, about 78 percent of households owned their homes or were paying one off.

That history explains what a buyer finds inside a typical house: compact lots, frame houses and flats built close together, and many decades of owners making their own repairs. Polish families gave way over time to immigrants from Yemen, Bangladesh, Pakistan and the Balkans, and a 2018 survey found schoolchildren speaking 16 native languages. Houses that changed hands inside one family for generations often carry unrecorded repairs, old liens or unclear titles, so clear those up before you pick an asking price.

How big are Hamtramck households, and what do homes cost?

Survey estimates covering 2020 through 2024 paint an unusual picture. Treat them as a starting point for pricing, not a final answer.

  • Typical owner-occupied home value: $131,000.
  • Homeownership: 58.3 percent among 7,120 households.
  • Persons per household: 3.86, which points to large households and heavily used kitchens and baths.
  • Typical rent: $989 a month.
  • Foreign-born residents make up 46.7 percent of the city, and 73.5 percent of people age 5 and over speak another language at home.

Because of those household sizes, a house with extra bedrooms or a finished basement often draws more interest than the same square footage elsewhere. Say plainly in your listing or conversation which rooms are legal bedrooms.

Must I pass a city inspection to sell in Hamtramck?

Only for some owners. Under the city's pre-sale subchapter (sections 150.201 to 150.206), a property holding a Neighborhood Enterprise Zone certificate cannot change hands, through a broker or otherwise, unless the Building Department has issued a current certificate of approval. Everyone else may request a voluntary inspection, but once you file that request you cannot withdraw it, and every violation found must be fixed to earn the certificate.

The same code gives you a way through if repairs would delay closing. The city refuses a transfer affidavit for an NEZ home that lacks the certificate, with one exception: the buyer may sign a notarized statement promising to fix every listed violation within six months. A few more details matter:

  • Both the inspection report and the certificate of approval last twelve months.
  • If the building official sees serious neglect or hazards, a mandatory inspection can be ordered whatever the NEZ status.
  • A certificate guarantees nothing about condition; the city accepts no liability for concealed defects, mold or asbestos.

Before signing a purchase agreement, call the Building Department and ask whether your parcel has an NEZ certificate.

What if the house is vacant, foreclosed or a rental?

Chapter 96 of the city code covers houses that have sat empty. A home vacant for 180 days or more, or one that any lender, county or other holder has foreclosed, cannot be occupied until the Department of Public Services issues a certificate of occupancy. Getting it takes an inspection, correction of every violation, and payment of back property tax, special assessments, water and sewer bills and city cleanup charges.

Rentals fall under Chapter 150. Landlords hold a certificate of compliance good for two years at first and three years at each renewal. A sale ends that certificate at once, and the buyer has 30 days after the ownership change to apply for a new one. A landlord with a notice of violation outstanding must hand the buyer a copy and file the buyer's notarized acknowledgment with the building official before conveying the property, land contracts included.

What are the Hamtramck tax deadlines, and what happens after them?

Bills come out on July 1 and December 1 and are paid at the city treasurer's office. Whatever remains after the city's February 28 cutoff passes to the Wayne County Treasurer, where the cost climbs. The table follows a parcel that stays unpaid.

Hamtramck and Wayne County tax calendar for an unpaid parcel
StageWhat happens
July 1Summer bill issued; full payment due August 20, or half in July with the rest by December 30
December 1Winter bill issued; due by February 15
February 28Final day to pay the city treasurer
March 1County takes over collection: a 4 percent fee plus 1 percent interest every month
March 1, a year after thatParcel forfeits; a $175 fee applies and monthly interest climbs to 1.5 percent
March 31 and April 1, a year after forfeitureCourt judgment; ownership moves to the county unless the owner redeems

Source: Hamtramck Treasurer and Wayne County Treasurer timeline pages. Foreclosed homes are then offered at public auction in September and October, so a seller with two years of arrears has a hard deadline.

What paperwork does the assessor need after a Hamtramck sale?

Buyers have 45 days after closing to file a Property Transfer Affidavit with the assessor; late filers can be charged $5 a day, capped at $200. Sellers sign a rescission request for their principal residence exemption so the claim leaves the parcel, since a missed rescission can turn into a bill if the state audits. A buyer who moves in files a fresh exemption affidavit, worth 18 mills of school operating tax.

State law also uncaps taxable value on a sale (MCL 211.27a): for the next calendar year it equals the state equalized value, roughly half of market price, which can push the buyer's first bill above yours. Assessment appeals go to the March Board of Review.

What transfer tax applies to a Hamtramck deed?

Michigan puts the transfer tax on the seller: $3.75 per $500 of price at the state level (MCL 207.525) plus a county levy under MCL 207.504 of 55 cents per $500 below 2,000,000 residents, capped at 75 cents above that. The county treasurer collects both within 15 days after the deed is handed over.

MCL 207.526 exempts family conveyances to a child or grandchild, judgments that name no price, and deeds issued in foreclosing government-backed loans. Confirm the county rate and the recording fee with Wayne County before closing.

Does Hamtramck have a local income tax I should plan for?

Yes. Hamtramck is one of the Michigan cities with its own income tax, at 1.00 percent for residents and 0.50 percent for nonresidents. Ask the city income tax office how a move out of town or rental income affects your filing.

More questions about Hamtramck, MI

Is a certificate of approval mandatory for my Hamtramck sale?

Only when the property holds a Neighborhood Enterprise Zone certificate. Other owners may ask for a voluntary inspection, though a filed request cannot be pulled back. In an NEZ sale, a buyer can offer a notarized repair promise in place of the certificate.

When is the Hamtramck summer tax bill due?

August 20 for the full amount. Paying half in July moves the rest to December 30. Winter bills are due February 15, and unpaid balances pass to Wayne County on March 1.

What is the foreclosure timeline for unpaid Hamtramck taxes?

About two years. Roughly two years from the first delinquency. Wayne County takes over on March 1, forfeits the parcel a year later, and a circuit court judgment follows. Owners can redeem through March 31 of the foreclosure year by paying taxes, interest and fees.

Which forms follow a Hamtramck closing?

The buyer files a transfer affidavit within 45 days, and the seller files a rescission of the principal residence exemption. A buyer who will live there also files a new exemption affidavit.

Does a Hamtramck rental certificate carry over to a buyer?

It does not. The certificate ends at the sale, and the new owner applies for another within 30 days of the ownership change.

Why does the inspection step set the pace of a Garden City sale?

A house cannot change occupants in Garden City until the city issues a certificate of occupancy, so the inspection calendar often matters more than the buyer's financing. The city is a compact Wayne County suburb of 5.87 square miles, roughly 15 miles west of downtown Detroit. A seller who books that inspection early can build the closing around it.

The notes below cover the inspection, the permit rules behind repairs, the city's housing figures, schools and services, and what follows a transfer of title.

How did Garden City get its layout and its name?

The name echoes the English garden city movement of the nineteenth century, and most early home sites were laid out as one-acre plots so a family could raise its own fruit and vegetables. Garden City became a village within Nankin Township in June 1927 and a city six years later. Most lots are now far smaller, some only 40 by 135 feet.

Counts climbed from 9,012 in 1950 to 38,017 in 1960 and topped out at 41,864 in 1970, before easing to 27,380 in 2020. Local landmarks include the site of the first Kmart, which opened in 1962 and has since been demolished, and Henry Ford's honeymoon cottage, moved here from Dearborn in 1952. Downtown centers on the corner of Ford and Middlebelt Roads.

  • The city's population quadrupled between 1950 and 1960, so much of the housing is now more than 60 years old.
  • Lots as small as 40 by 135 feet leave little room for additions or large outbuildings.
  • Ford Road and Middlebelt Road are the main corridors for commuting and errands.

How many Garden City homes are owner-occupied, and what are they worth?

This is a city of homeowners: QuickFacts shows nearly four of every five homes occupied by their owners.

Headcount slipped 4.1% from the April 2020 base, so a seller should not wait for a wave of newcomers. A price that reflects the house's true condition moves a sale along faster.

How does the Garden City certificate of occupancy work for a seller?

Whenever a property is sold, the city wants a certificate of occupancy in place before the buyer moves in. The Building Department schedules the inspection, which takes place Monday through Thursday, with a morning window from 9 a.m. to noon and an afternoon window from noon to 4 p.m. The department's FAQ lists a $200 fee, payable when the inspection date is booked, and says the certificate is good for one year.

The city warns that spring and summer are the busy season, and that a seller may wait three to six weeks for an inspection. Someone who needs a fast closing should reserve the slot the day a contract is signed, or sooner. The Building Department number is (734) 793-1650.

  • Reserve an inspection date when the home is listed or under contract.
  • Fix visible safety items first, since a failed inspection means a reinspection and more waiting.
  • The city's FAQ suggests a December or January certificate is ready for an immediate closing.

Which repairs need a permit in Garden City?

A permit is good for six months, and all inspections must happen inside that window. Roof, windows, exterior doors, siding, gutters and kitchen or bathroom remodels need a building permit. Water tanks, furnaces, air conditioners and generators need mechanical permits. Service panels, circuits, fixtures and hard-wired smoke detectors need electrical permits, and sewer repairs, sinks, toilets and showers need plumbing permits. Driveways, easement walks, patios and porch caps fall under a flatwork permit.

Sheds under 200 square feet need no building permit but still need a flatwork permit for the slab. An owner living in the house may pull personal permits, and anyone who hires a contractor should require the contractor to pull them, at the same cost. Ask the Building Department whether any open permit on the address could affect the certificate before you list.

What happens if the house is a rental?

Garden City runs a rental certification program through its Ordinance Department at the police department, reachable at (734) 793-1748. Rental certifications run three years, and the owner must recertify before the term ends. A landlord selling the house should confirm that the certification is current and say whether tenants will stay.

An investor buying it should ask the Ordinance Department how the transfer affects that certification.

What do schools and city services add to a Garden City listing?

The Garden City School District runs four elementary schools, a middle school, Garden City High School, home of the Cougars, and Cambridge High School as its alternative program. Tipton Academy, a charter school, serves pre-kindergarten through seventh grade. St. Raphael Catholic School closed in 2016, and the former Radcliff Middle School building became a recreation center the city bought from Schoolcraft College.

Residents receive a free 95-gallon trash container from the city's refuse contractor, and curbside recycling carts can be delivered on request. Yard waste pickup runs from the first full week of April until about the middle of December, with Christmas trees collected after December 25. Buyers ask about such basics, so mention them when you describe the property.

What does the Michigan transfer tax cost on a Garden City sale?

Michigan's two transfer taxes, both paid by the seller, are 55 cents for the county and $3.75 for the state on every $500 of price (MCL 207.504 and 207.525). The county treasurer collects within 15 days after the deed is delivered (MCL 207.523).

A sale at Garden City's median value of $168,800 owes roughly $1,460, and the settlement statement shows the exact figure. The buyer then notifies the assessor within 45 days so taxable value can reset to the state equalized value the next year (MCL 211.27a). Ask the assessor for an estimate of the new owner's bill.

When does an as-is sale make sense for a Garden City house?

A small, well-kept house on a standard lot can sell through a listing, though the inspection queue and the buyer's loan both add time. A house that needs work to pass the certificate of occupancy, an estate property, or a seller facing a short deadline often does better with an as-is purchase.

  • A listing fits a house in good repair when you can wait out the inspection queue.
  • An as-is buyer fits a house where the inspector will likely list repairs you would rather not manage.
  • Get written agreement on who pays the inspection fee and handles any reinspection.

Weigh offers by what you keep after transfer tax, prorated taxes and credits, and write the closing date into the contract.

More questions about Garden City, MI

Must a Garden City house pass inspection before it changes hands?

Yes. The city requires a certificate of occupancy whenever a property is sold, and the new owner cannot occupy the house without it. The Building Department at (734) 793-1650 books the inspection.

How long is the wait for the Garden City inspection?

The city says a seller may wait three to six weeks in spring and summer. Booking early, or aiming for winter, shortens the wait.

What does the Garden City certificate of occupancy cost?

The city's FAQ lists $200, paid when the inspection is scheduled, for a certificate good for one year. Confirm the amount with the Building Department.

Will a Garden City buyer's tax bill run higher than mine?

Often. Taxable value resets to the state equalized value in the calendar year after the transfer, and the buyer must notify the assessor within 45 days.

Can I still sell a house that fails the inspection?

Yes, but the certificate has to be issued before the new owner moves in. Some sellers make the repairs, and others sell as-is and let the buyer finish them and request the reinspection.
